title: Cocompleteness and tensor-compatible homotopy colimits of dg model localizations
statement:
Use coherent diagrams, mapping spaces, equivalences and limiting or colimiting cocones as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. In particular, coherent diagrams are simplicial maps into quasicategories, transformations are edges of the internal functor simplicial set, and colimiting cocones are initial objects of the coherent comma cocone category, using its right-pinched mapping spaces and weak contractibility. A diagram indexed by an ordinary category $J$ means a diagram on its nerve $N(J)$. Use cochain complexes, quasi-isomorphisms and the derived category convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use locally presentable in the explicit sense of [lem-coef-accessible-monad-presentability]. Fix universes large enough for all categories and small diagram shapes in this statement. Let $\mathcal M$ be a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category, enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups. Suppose there are retract-closed classes $C,F,W$, with $W$ satisfying two-out-of-three, and functorial weak factorization systems $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ generated by sets. A weak factorization system means every map factors as a map of the first class followed by one of the second, and the two classes are exactly each other's diagonal-lifting classes. Assume the enriched model axiom: for $i:A\to B$ in $C$ and $p:X\to Y$ in $F$, the map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,X)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,X)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,Y)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,Y)$$
is degreewise surjective, and a quasi-isomorphism if $i$ or $p$ belongs to $W$. Let $\mathcal D=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$ be the enriched localization of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal], with derived mapping objects $R\operatorname{Hom}$.

The underlying infinity category of $\mathcal D$ has all small limits and colimits. Its enrichment is tensored over the enhanced derived category $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$: for $K\in\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$ and $X\in\mathcal D$ the derived tensor $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}X$ exists, satisfies the tensor--mapping-object adjunction, and preserves small colimits in each variable. For every small homotopy coherent diagram $A:J\to\mathcal D$ and $Y\in\mathcal D$, its colimit cocone induces an equivalence
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(\operatorname{colim}_J A,Y)\simeq\operatorname{lim}_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(A_j,Y)$$
in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$, natural in $A,Y$. Both sides retain the coherent structure maps; these are homotopy limits and colimits. For $J=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, where $\Delta$ has finite nonempty ordered sets and order-preserving maps, the colimit is the geometric realization and the displayed limit is the derived totalization. Finally $W$ is saturated: an actual morphism of $\mathcal M$ belongs to $W$ if and only if its image in the underlying infinity category of $\mathcal D$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Agent-formulated general dg-model foundation for paragraph 2. WANTED: the derived-enriched tensor and colimit theorem for combinatorial dg model categories. Lurie, Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 1.3.4.22, Propositions 1.3.4.23-24 and Corollary 1.3.4.26 give presentability, homotopy (co)limit comparison and left-Quillen colimit preservation on underlying infinity categories; read online https://people.math.harvard.edu/~lurie/papers/HA.pdf, printed pp. 118-120, not archived. The derived chain-enriched tensor and mapping-object formulation remains an explicit unsplit foundation. Model saturation is the standard model-localization assertion, also mentioned in Harpaz, Lax limits of model categories (2018 version), Remark 10. No Stacks tag states this whole enriched result.
